detail.abstract: Recovery from addiction is often described as a change in behavior, motivation, or personal identity. Social recognition, however, does not always change at the same pace. A person may reduce or stop substance use, rebuild routines, and assume new responsibilities while continuing to be treated primarily as "the addict," "the patient," or "the person at risk." This article develops the concept of borrowed identity to describe an identity that is socially authored, maintained, and applied through family memory, professional language, institutional records, recovery cultures, and reputational expectations. The concept neither denies the harms associated with substance use nor dismisses legitimate caution. It identifies a temporal and relational problem in which behavioral change precedes revision of the categories used to interpret the person. Drawing on social identity theory, labeling and stigma scholarship, family research, recovery capital, mutualhelp research, and qualitative studies of treatment experience, the article argues that recovery remains socially incomplete until recognition, trust, and autonomy are renegotiated. The Relational Identity Release Framework organizes this analysis around recognition lag, identity compression, surveillance density, plurality of belonging, and restitution of autonomy. It is offered as a heuristic for psychosocial research and practice rather than as a diagnostic instrument. Recovery requires more than leaving a pattern of use. It also requires conditions under which the person can become socially legible as more than that pattern.

title: Conjugate Priors for Families Said to Have None
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Conjugate Priors for Families Said to Have None
detail.abstract: Many standard families are described as having no conjugate prior. We argue that the description conflates three different failures, only one of which is an impossibility theorem, and that the remaining two are solved by a single construction. Writing the parameterdependent part of the likelihood as exp(t ⊤ θ)g(θ)-1 and giving the prior the same shape, the Diaconis-Ylvisaker propriety theorem supplies, in one statement, both the condition for the prior to be proper and the elicitation identity for its hyperparameters. We record three structural consequences that appear not to be collected anywhere: the resulting conjugate family is itself an exponential family with natural parameter (t 0 , c) and sufficient statistic (θ,-A(θ)), it is log-concave in the natural parameterisation, and its marginal likelihood is a ratio of two normalising constants. We also give a boundary-corrected elicitation identity, and show by a worked example on the exponentially tilted stable family that the openness hypothesis in the Diaconis-Ylvisaker theorem is not decorative: there the mean-parameter identity fails by exactly the reciprocal of the normalising constant, a discrepancy we confirm numerically to ten digits. Specialising g recovers the reciprocal gamma prior for the gamma shape, the Boatwright et al. propriety condition for Conway-Maxwell-Poisson, the Stirlinggamma and Pochhammer priors for gamma-ratio concentration parameters, and a reciprocal zeta prior for the Zipf exponent. We grade the resulting conjugacies by whether the prior family has fixed dimension, is indexed by the sample size, or grows with it.

title: Rational Conjugacy: Pochhammer Priors and Gamma Ratios
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Rational Conjugacy: Pochhammer Priors and Gamma Ratios
detail.abstract: Pochhammer priors, introduced by Wang and Polson (2024), give conjugate Bayesian inference for concentration parameters that enter a likelihood through ratios of Gamma functions with integer shifts. This paper develops the general theory of that family around a single principle, rational conjugacy: the Pochhammer family is not closed under Bayesian updating, but the proper rational densities on R + are, and on that class every normalizing constant, moment and predictive probability is a finite sum of residues. Five results follow, each generalizing or correcting a statement of Wang and Polson (2024). A general residue formula admits poles of arbitrary multiplicity anywhere in the cut plane, as required for Pitman–Yor, where poles repeat, and for Erlang’s loss system, where they are complex. The Mellin transform of a Pochhammer density is obtained in closed form on its maximal strip, delivering fractional and negative moments, Elogα, the exact tail index b − m − d − 1 (with a second, probabilistic proof in Corollary 9), and a corrected reading of the Kullback–Leibler risk bound: every m attains the super-efficient rate N −1 logN, and m = 0 merely minimizes the constant. A completely monotone representation then identifies m = d = 0 on structural grounds: the half-horseshoe is a scale mixture of exponentials whose mixing law is a size-debiased sum of independent exponentials, so a latent scale reduces the prior to a tilt exactly as an inverse-Gamma scale reduces the half-Cauchy to a Gaussian. The consequence is practical. Wherever a Gamma prior on a concentration parameter admits an exact draw, the half-horseshoe does too, at the cost of b extra exponential variates; for Negative Binomial regression this yields a Gibbs sampler in which every block is a standard draw, no Metropolis step appears, and no residue is ever evaluated. An exponentially tilted family completes the picture, its normalizer a finite sum of exponential integrals, and the tilt removes the degree restriction b ≥ m+d +2 altogether. We then locate the boundary of the method: Γ(α + u)/Γ(α + v) is rational if and only if u−v ∈ Z, so Damsleth’s (1975) conjugate class for the two-parameter Gamma lies outside it, and we give three exact repairs, of which Poisson augmentation is the sharpest, together with a fourth that is not ours: the reciprocal Gamma mixtures of He, Polson and Xu reach the transcendental factor directly, and we set out the division of labour between augmentation and residues. A power-law theorem shows the Negative Binomial–Beta–Pochhammer hierarchy generates p(n) ∼ Kn−(1+a) (logn) −{2+1(m≥1)} , so a Zipf exponent may be elicited as a prior hyperparameter. Applications include Polya urns, the Ewens sampling formula, Pitman–Yor concentration, Yule processes ´ and Erlang’s formula, and a Negative Binomial regression study of two count data sets in which a Ga(2,1) prior on the dispersion excludes the maximum likelihood value by a factor of four and doubles the width of the predictive bands, while the half-horseshoe does not. Finally we quantify a limitation: the residue expansion is exact but ill conditioned, provably losing nlog10 2 digits in a solvable case, and we give three remedies.

title: Thorin Measures and Zeta Zeros
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Thorin Measures and Zeta Zeros
detail.abstract: Recent experiments realise the nontrivial zeros of ζ as dynamical quantum phase transitions, with Re(s) an inverse temperature and Im(s) an evolution time. That is the pairing which organises Thorin’s representation of a generalised gamma convolution, and this paper develops the consequences. The Gibbs state in those experiments is the Riemann zeta distribution: its characteristic function is ζ(β + it)/ζ(β), the Euler product is a Levy–Khintchine exponent, unique factorisation is the decomposition of that law into independent prime power jumps, and no transition can occur for Re(s) > 1 because infinitely divisible characteristic functions do not vanish. The main result is that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if Φ(λ) = ξ(1/2)/ξ(1/2 + √ λ) is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution, necessarily that of X = P k Ek/γ2 k with Ek independent standard exponentials. The Thorin measure is the zero counting measure pushed forward by squaring, with density (4π √ v) −1 log( √ v/2π); the Levy density is x −1Θ(x) with Θ the heat trace of the conjectural Hilbert–Polya operator; the cumulants are (m − 1)!P k γ −2m k ; and − log Φ(λ) ∼ πN( √ λ), whence − log P(X ≤ ε) ∼ log2 (1/ε)/16ε. Second quantisation unifies the picture: 1/Φ is the free fermion partition function of a gas with single particle weights γ −2 k and Φ the free boson one, their Taylor coefficients being the elementary and complete homogeneous symmetric functions of those weights, so the hypothesis says exactly that the weights are positive. The fermionic side is a Polya frequency condition, which places the Turan inequalities and the Jensen polynomial results in this frame; the bosonic side is a Stieltjes moment condition computable from ξ at the central point without any zeros, and verified here through order six. On the apparatus side the probe qubit measures a characteristic function, its dephasing bath spectral density is the Levy measure, and the probe’s time reversal symmetry is the involution whose quotient defines the Thorin variable. These are equivalences rather than a proof strategy, and the circularity that would have to be broken is stated explicitly.

title: From Marriage Economics to Multi-Nomoi Governance: A Dialectical Generative Relational Economics Perspective

detail.title: From Marriage Economics to Multi-Nomoi Governance: A Dialectical Generative Relational Economics Perspective
detail.abstract: A marriage is commonly assessed under two orders of value at once. One takes the endowments of the parties as given and asks how they are to be arranged; the other takes as its object what the coupling produces over time. The parties to such a disagreement ordinarily describe it as a difference of values. This paper locates a further difference, which is a difference of evidence regime: the first order is verifiable in advance by third parties, and the second is verifiable in retrospect and largely from inside the relation. From that difference two results follow. The first is a derivation: the burden of translating between two orders of value falls on the party whose order is verifiable only in retrospect, so that weakness of position accompanies the burden without constituting its mechanism; a corollary holds that remaking the retrospective order into an ex ante checkable form returns part of the burden and converts what it measures. The second is a device: integration across two orders can proceed by warranting, in which one party supplies a guarantee stated in the currency of the other while the substantive claim stays unconverted, and this device is distinguished here from translation, from commensuration, from compromise, and from the interface norms of legal pluralism. The paper moves from the marital case, where both orders happen to be economies of value, to the general case, where an order may be religious, customary, professional or juridical, for which the term nomos is adopted and given a three-part definition whose third component is verification. European institutions supply the case material, organised by device: the equal authenticity of language versions, mutual recognition and its documented difficulties, conditional recognition on a guarantee of equivalent protection, coordination by indicator, pledge structures under expert monitoring, subsidiarity review, and the margin of appreciation. Inclusion is then stated as the holding of a claim that is never required to be converted into the dominant currency of evaluation.

title: Non-Monotonic Fertility Dynamics, External Childcare Services, and Economic Development

detail.title: Non-Monotonic Fertility Dynamics, External Childcare Services, and Economic Development

declarations.funderStatement: The author gratefully acknowledges the financial support of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research from the JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number 22K13407.

detail.abstract: This study develops an overlapping generations model with Stone-Geary preferences and external childcare services to clarify the mechanisms underlying non-monotonic fertility dynamics recently observed in developed countries. We show that non-monotonic fertility dynamics emerge with economic development when the elasticity of substitution between consumption and the number of children is sufficiently large and the cost of external childcare services is neither too low nor too high: specifically, the Malthusian regime, modern growth regime, fertility rebound regime, and renewed fertility decline regime historically observed in developed countries. This study also investigates that fertility dynamics and economic development are strongly influenced by both the elasticity of substitution and the cost of external childcare services. Higher values of these factors tend to result in lower fertility and greater capital per capita. Furthermore, faster productivity growth in the childcare sector lowers the relative price of childcare services, prolongs the fertility rebound, and increases output per capita.

title: The Price of Full Reserve: What a Datacenter Battery Gives up to Stay Always Ready, on Nine Years of Japanese Market Data

detail.title: The Price of Full Reserve: What a Datacenter Battery Gives up to Stay Always Ready, on Nine Years of Japanese Market Data

detail.abstract: The AI datacenter is rebuilding its power chain into tiers of storage, and the largest tier-the facility-scale battery that grows out of the UPS-is the first that could earn revenue in electricity markets. Whether it may is governed by one inherited habit: the backup reserve is held in full, at all times. This paper prices that habit on nine fiscal years of Japanese public data-outage statistics, diesel field reliability, balancingmarket and day-ahead prices. Full reservation costs a battery between 1% and 37% of achievable arbitrage value, depending on its diesel-coverage window and grid-contract headroom; at the conservative corner it is a nearly constant 37-41% share of market value across nine years spanning an 8× revenue range. What it buys is small: even a battery that ignores its reserve entirely accumulates about 0.1 min of expected downtime per year at Japanese interruption rates; against an implementable risk-budgeted reservation that never surrenders the bridging reserve, holding full reserve breaks even only above roughly ¥50 billion per avoided event. The design space is forgiving: Japan's primary frequency-response product is deliverable at full rating from the reserve floor itself-also the slowest-ageing posture-and deep participation needs only a spread threshold calibrated on the previous year, capturing 94-100% of the risk-budget frontier within a price regime and 64% across the sharpest regime exit. At every design point examined, the inherited answer is the most expensive one on the table.

title: An Unconditional Euler Factorisation: The M¨Obius Laplace Transform as a Generalised Gamma Convolution
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: An Unconditional Euler Factorisation: The M¨Obius Laplace Transform as a Generalised Gamma Convolution
detail.abstract: The previous notes ended with criteria, not theorems. Here is the unconditional part of the story. On the ζ side the Lévy datum is the von Mangoldt measure, which is nonnegative, so the transport applies verbatim and the Euler product splits it into independent factors, one per prime. We introduce a single universal one-parameter family K q , 0 < q < 1, with completely explicit Laplace transform, Thorin density τ q (y) = q(1+q) π(1-q) • 1-cos √ 2y √ 2y |1-qe i √ 2y | 2 , mean q/(1-q) 2 and infinite variance, and prove: for every α > 1 and every s ≥ 0, ζ(α)e s(ζ ′ /ζ)(α) n≥1 µ(n)n-α-s = E[exp(-1 2 s 2 H α)] with H α = p (log p) 2 K p-α a sum of independent generalised gamma convolutions. The Möbius series is therefore, after tilting, a Laplace transform in the squared variable, and the Euler product is the independence structure of H α. The same holds for the completed function without its pole factor, with an explicit archimedean factor k≥1 (1 + s α+2k)e-s/(α+2k) , and for any Euler product with nonnegative von Mangoldt coefficients, and for every truncated Euler product at every α > 0. We close with the exact identity for ξ, in which the entire negative contribution is the single explicit term w 2 / (α-1)((α-1) 2 + w 2) coming from the pole, and with a candid statement of what this does and does not give.

title: A Signed Thorin Version of the L´Evy-To-Thorin Lemma: Quasi-Infinite Divisibility and Positivity Uplift
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Signed Thorin Version of the L´Evy-To-Thorin Lemma: Quasi-Infinite Divisibility and Positivity Uplift
detail.abstract: Lemma 1 of the companion note transports a Lévy representation of log f (α + s)/f (α) into a Thorin representation in the squared variable s 2 /2, via a sine-squared kernel, and concludes that the resulting density να is completely monotone. Nothing in the transport uses positivity of µ. We record the signed version, Lemma 1 ′ , in which να is a difference of completely monotone functions and the associated law is at most quasi-infinitely divisible. The signed statement has no structural value on its own, since quasi-infinitely divisible laws are weakly dense. Its use lies in the opposite direction: the sine-squared kernel is strictly positivity improving, so να ≥ 0 is genuinely weaker than µ ≥ 0. We give a verifiable sufficient condition for this uplift, an explicit example in which a signed Thorin datum yields a bona fide generalised gamma convolution, and the branch obstruction that prevents any quasi version from shortening the argument.

title: Classical and Quantum Equilibria in Bayesian Games ⋆
affiliations: University of Rochester

detail.title: Classical and Quantum Equilibria in Bayesian Games ⋆
detail.abstract: Players in a Bayesian game are forbidden to share their private signals with anyone, including a referee; each player can condition her action only on phenomena she observes directly. We classify Bayes correlated equilibria by the resources required to implement them privately. Some arise from strategic-form correlated equilibria and can be implemented by a signal-blind referee. A strictly larger class can be implemented with classical correlating devices: we exhibit an equilibrium implementable by such devices but by no referee, strengthening a known separation between strategic-form and agent-normal-form correlated equilibrium. A larger class still becomes implementable with quantum devices, and quantum-implementable equilibria can be Pareto-superior to every classical equilibrium-even in games where the players' interests conflict. The paper presupposes no familiarity with quantum mechanics and is intended to double as an introduction to quantum game theory for economists.

title: Who Attests the Attestor? Evidentiary Independence as a Missing Property of Vertically Integrated AI Systems
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Who Attests the Attestor? Evidentiary Independence as a Missing Property of Vertically Integrated AI Systems
detail.abstract: Some of the most capable artificial-intelligence systems now operate inside conglomerates that control the model, the platform on which it acts, the user-facing payment interface through which it transacts, the process that reviews disputes about its conduct, and the records that memorialize those activities. Computer science has made real progress on one property of such records: integrity, the assurance that alteration after capture is detectable. This paper argues that a second property has often been mistaken for the first. Evidentiary independence, the degree to which capture, custody, and disclosure do not rest exclusively with an interested party, has no settled treatment in the literature reviewed here. A tamperevident log controlled by the party it implicates establishes only that committed entries were not changed after commitment. It says nothing by itself about whether capture was complete, whether the source was accurate, or whether content was selectively withheld. Drawing on the economics of auditing, the treatment of self-serving records in evidence law, and the 2025 to 2026 operational history of one highly integrated AI-centered enterprise group, the paper formalizes the distinction between the two properties; explains why consolidation can erode independence even while improving integrity; identifies control handoffs between humans and machines, in autonomous vehicles and agentic payments, as a setting where the erosion matters acutely; proposes a four-level taxonomy of attestation regimes; specifies minimal requirements for independent receipts under a strict claim discipline; and shows how independence can be made quantitative. Modeled as a graph of evidence paths attributed with control domains, a fact's evidentiary independence degree is the minimum number of domains whose joint failure or self-interested withholding severs every path capable of establishing it. This renders the evidentiary cost of consolidation computable and permits autonomous operation to be conditioned on machine-verified evidentiary fitness. An independent commitment receipt can later establish that a disclosed record matches a bitstring committed no later than an independently observed time, that the commitment left the operator's exclusive control, and, through declared coverage discipline, whether the record class was continuously submitted. It does not establish the truth of the record, the time of the underlying event, or complete capture. It is a receipt, not a verdict.

title: Thorin Positivity for Dirichlet L-Functions
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Thorin Positivity for Dirichlet L-Functions
detail.abstract: For ζ the L´evy datum of the Bernstein-to-Thorin transport is the von Mangoldt measure, which is nonnegative, and everything is a theorem. For a Dirichlet L-function with non-principal character the primes split into those where χ = +1 and those where χ = −1, the datum is signed, and the transport delivers not a generalised gamma convolution but a quotient of two. We show this is not a defect of the method, and we compute the failure exactly. Because Φf α is a sum over primes of continuous 2π-periodic functions of w log p, and the log p are Q-independent, Kronecker’s theorem localises the extrema: the global infimum is the sum of the local infima. Evaluating those in closed form gives, for every non-principal real χ mod q and every α > 1, inf w Φ L α(w) = −2 X p: χ(p)=−1 p α log p p 2α − 1 = ζ (q)′ ζ (q) (α) − L ′ L (α, χ) < 0, with a companion formula for the supremum, neither attained. Since L(s, χ) has no zeros to the right of 1, Thorin positivity is strictly stronger than a zero-free half-plane. The quotient structure is explicit: factors with χ(p) = +1 multiply by a generalised gamma convolution Kq, those with χ(p) = −1 divide by one, Keq, the Thorin densities differing only by q 7→ −q, and a single closed form covers these and all complex characters with local sign sign Re χ(p). The constructive half of the paper concerns the completed Λ(s, χ), entire with no pole factor. Its criterion reads Aα+P χ α ≥ 0 with Aα archimedean, positive and ∼ 1 2 log w, and P χ α bounded below by the exact constant above. There is no near-total cancellation, and the criterion at α > 1 reduces to an explicit compact window: for χ mod 4 at α = 2 the whole question lives on 0.12 ≤ w ≤ 4.48. Numerically ΦΛ α > 0 throughout, for seven characters, for w to 4000 including resonant frequencies, and for every α tested down to 0.51.

title: Thorin, Levy and Mobius: Sign Structure in the Reciprocals of ξ and ζ
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Thorin, Levy and Mobius: Sign Structure in the Reciprocals of ξ and ζ
detail.abstract: This note follows a single question through three charts: what does taking a reciprocal cost? On ℜs > 1 the positive object is ζ itself, which Khinchine read as a compound Poisson Laplace transform; we show that its reciprocal is the convolution exponential of the negated prime Levy measure, so that the Mobius function is literally a negated Levy density, factoring as an infinite convolution of two point signed atoms with squarefree support and sign (-1) ω(n) as consequences rather than inputs. On the real segment 1 2 < σ < 1, where the representation need only hold for the Riemann Hypothesis, we show that the restriction to real arguments loses nothing but cannot deliver a positivity criterion, since the limit has the opposite sign to the leading term, the Euler product diverges to zero, and both positive halves of the Mobius measure have abscissa exactly one by Landau's theorem. Adding the archimedean factors decomposes the exponent of 1/ξ at the critical line into four Laplace type pieces, one of which has the explicit completely monotone density e-5u/2 /(1-e-2u) with Thorin atoms on the trivial zeros; none has the right sign, and their defects cancel only jointly, leaving a function of s 2. Folding by that square map yields a Thorin representation of 1/ξ(1 2 + √ s) which exists unconditionally, with Thorin measure carried by the squared zero displacements. A 2 sin 2 lemma then shows the Levy density to be always a completely monotone function minus a nonnegative defect, and the Riemann Hypothesis to be equivalent to nonnegativity of the Thorin measure and to complete monotonicity of that density, though not of the transform. Applied across the three charts the same half angle identity is nonnegative in each, so the arithmetic lies not in the identity but in whether the defect enters additively or subtractively. Two unconditional statements result. First, F is always a quotient of two infinitely divisible Laplace transforms, the numerator a generalised gamma convolution and the denominator an explicit factor that degenerates exactly under the hypothesis. Second, the Thorin moments are computable from ξ alone, and the hypothesis is equivalent to nonnegativity of the two Hankel determinant families built from them; read in the square variable, the real segment carries precisely this moment sequence, which is why an unconditional criterion is available there and not in the prime chart.

title:
A Positive Law with M¨Obius Weights

First Passage Superpositions and Unconditional Inequalities for Pµ(N)N −S
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title:
A Positive Law with M¨Obius Weights

First Passage Superpositions and Unconditional Inequalities for Pµ(N)N −S
detail.abstract: The Bernstein-to-Thorin transport turns ζ(α)/ζ(α + s) into a Laplace transform in the squared variable s 2 /2. Since the reciprocal of ζ is the Möbius series, and since e-ℓ √ 2u is the Laplace transform of the Brownian first passage time T ℓ , that transform inverts term by term. Writing ℓ n = log n-(ζ ′ /ζ)(α) > 0, the law H α attached to ζ at α > 1 is a signed superposition of stable-1 2 laws, with an explicit density. Positivity of a signed superposition is a theorem, not an accident, and it yields a master family of unconditional inequalities, one for each nonnegative test function, which is equivalent to the transport theorem rather than weaker than it. We then ask which members of that family carry content, and the answer is a dichotomy of contours. Setting F (v) = e vcα /ζ(α + v), the completely monotone members and the power family S(θ) = n µ(n)n-α ℓ θ n are both integrals of 1/ζ along the real half-line, positive because ζ > 0 there and F is decreasing, the latter needing only Cauchy-Schwarz on the Dirichlet series of ζ. This gives S(θ) > 0 for θ < 1, S(1) = 0 and, after one further step, S(θ) < 0 for 1 < θ < 3, the sign change being the pole of Γ(-θ); all negative and fractional positive moments of H α follow. The Gaussian weights are different: they are an integral of 1/ζ along the vertical line Re s = α, where the integrand oscillates. That is the only part of the master family that is not elementary, and by the converse it is exactly Λ ≥ 0. Finally we isolate the primitive V of the tail of the Möbius measure, prove a master real-axis identity expressing every such sum through V , and show that V is not nonnegative: an exact eight-term computation gives V (3) < 0 at α = 2. Two structural routes to the full sign pattern are thereby closed. We also state the signed transport, Lemma 1 ′ of the first note, as a theorem, record the moment identities S(1) = 0, S(2) =-(log ζ) ′′ /ζ and S(3) = (log ζ) ′′′ /ζ, and add two sharp facts obtained by localising the extrema over Euler factors: the exact value of sup w Φ ζ α , and the monotonicity of √ 2πt ν α (t).

title: On the Wallace Conjecture in a Scalable Zhu Economy

detail.title: On the Wallace Conjecture in a Scalable Zhu Economy
detail.abstract: We study the Wallace conjecture in a scalable version of Zhu's divisiblemoney random-matching economy. A proportional balance-contingent grant expands nominal balances, payments, and the individual ceiling together, leaving normalized balances, real allocations, and welfare unchanged. This exact neutrality isolates the effects of redistributing liquidity across balance states. Under truthful private reporting, local equilibrium-path regularity, and a primitiverank condition, complete first-order neutrality is confined to a lower-dimensional set of primitives; generically, some nearby feasible grant improves welfare. A two-direction application decomposes the welfare effect into direct-trade, continuation-value, and distribution channels, while a discretized calculation illustrates a positive effect.

title: Trajectory and Attribution in Generative Relational Systems: A Preliminary Position Paper on Datability, Criticality, and the Endogenous Predisposition

detail.title: Trajectory and Attribution in Generative Relational Systems: A Preliminary Position Paper on Datability, Criticality, and the Endogenous Predisposition
detail.abstract: In one class of injury a set of factors, each individually incapable of destabilising the injured system, acts over a long period, reduces its capacity to recover from disturbance, and permits a later disturbance of ordinary magnitude to produce a severe outcome. Doctrine processes multi-causal injury with tolerable success and processes this class badly, and the reason is one of representation rather than of proof. The paper isolates one requirement, named datability: a change of state carrying legal significance must be assignable to a point in time. A dynamical presentation of a bistable system under slow forcing shows that the onset of criticality withholds what the requirement demands, for two reasons that hold of the system rather than of the observer, and six doctrinal operations fail together with it. Four consequences follow. Each factor is necessary and the conjunction of all of them remains insufficient, so the but-for test and the balance of probabilities come apart and the refinement requiring a sufficient set survives only by admitting a term attributable to nobody. The antecedent conduct and the terminal disturbance are excluded by different doctrines, and the threshold that decides which acts leave a record is the threshold that decides which acts carry significance, so the two exclusions are one filter counted twice. The predisposition on which reduction doctrines operate is a product of the conduct at issue, so those doctrines deduct the quantity that constitutes the wrong. Near a boundary of stability the outcome is completed by the amplification of the injured system, which doctrine reads through two settled figures that both discharge the defendants. The paper then separates two limitations of the classical apparatus. One concerns the resources available for recording and interpreting a history and would be relieved by their extension. The other concerns what a determinate contribution would require, namely closure of the set of variables bearing on the case, a declared class of admissible trajectories, and identifiability of the couplings, and it is unaffected by any capacity of the tribunal. Against the second the paper proposes findings of position, whose value is fixed by the record where the quantities are not, and observes that such findings are binary as a verdict is binary. It closes with the migration of the case to supervisory obligation, the price of that migration, and one route that dispenses with the representation of trajectories. Conditions of refutation are given throughout.

title: The Thorin Transport
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Thorin Transport
detail.abstract: The Lévy-to-Thorin transport requires only real s > 0. On that half-line the branch of the logarithm is canonical, because ξ > 0 on R, and the whole content of the transport is a single kernel identity. We use this to identify the Lévy datum µ explicitly. The dictionary is (log f) ′′ (w) = ∞ 0 x e-wx µ(dx). For f = ζ this gives the von Mangoldt measure µ ζ = n≥2 Λ(n)δ log n ≥ 0, so Lemma 1 applies verbatim for α > 1 and delivers a genuine generalised gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin density. For f = ξ it gives µ ξ (dx) = (e 2x-1)-1-e x dx + n≥2 Λ(n)δ log n , a signed measure whose sign comes entirely from the pole factor 1 2 w(w-1), and whose spectral form is µ ξ (dx) =ρ e ρx dx; the equality of the two forms is the explicit formula. At the centre α = 1 2 the drift term vanishes, the transport becomes even in s, and ν 1/2 (t) = ℑρ>0 e (ρ-1/2) 2 t/2 , so complete monotonicity of ν 1/2 is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, with Thorin measure γ>0 δ γ 2 /2 and H 1/2 = γ>0 2E γ /γ 2. We give numerical verification, and we are explicit about the degeneration: the positivity criterion that is a smooth inequality for α > 1 collapses to the trivial identity 0 = 0 at the centre, because the criterion's density becomes a purely atomic measure carried by the zero ordinates.

title: Writing the Way Up: Benefit Calibration and the Honesty Window in Joint Verification

detail.title: Writing the Way Up: Benefit Calibration and the Honesty Window in Joint Verification
detail.abstract: An auditor chooses what it says-a committed disclosure experiment-and what it isa privately chosen capability-before a verifier who reads both at a conjecture. Under a liability read alone, a companion paper showed the two margins conspire: the sender certifies a capability it has quietly lowered, driving the read to a floor immune to detection and conjecture, and the pen that proves a capability writes downward. This paper adds the reward the liability literature holds fixed-the sender is also paid for being believed capableand prices it. Because the reward is affine in the believed capability, it folds into the liability read to form a single composite read, and the companion's theorems apply to it verbatim; what is new is where the reward's price carries that read. At a low price the pen writes down, the companion's sandbag; at a high price it writes up, capability built and proven; and between them lies an honesty window, an interval of prices in which the two directions cancel, the sender discloses nothing and is honest on average, and the joint conspiracyninety-two percent of the deviation gain in the companion-dissolves at zero instrument cost. A martingale identity keeps the reward out of the honest price of disclosure, so the window is the interval a single quadratic cuts; its exact location is inherited from the private-capability companion as a calibration ray that depends on the verifier's eyesight. Rational pricing does not break the window but widens it at every configuration tested, by a structural ordering of reliefs: no conjecture can punish silence, and the only reversal a conjecture opens is one of reward, because a friendly conjecture relieves only what passes through it and silence passes everything while proof passes nothing. The design lesson is that a calibrated reward is an instrument the earlier papers lacked-closing both margins at once, at an optimum where the incentive to game disappears-subject to the honest caveat that the window preserves capability without building it. The pen writes both ways; what decides the direction is not the hand that holds it but the price of the ink.

title: When the File is the Only Voice: Document Integrity as the Decisive Factor After the End of the Affirmative Asylum Interview

detail.title: When the File is the Only Voice: Document Integrity as the Decisive Factor After the End of the Affirmative Asylum Interview
detail.abstract: On July 27, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security published an interim final rule authorizing U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to refer affirmative asylum applications directly to immigration court without first conducting an interview. The rule follows, by exactly sixty-two days, the May 26, 2026 directive from DHS General Counsel James Percival instructing ICE attorneys to pursue immigration attorneys who file fraudulent asylum applications. This paper argues that the two measures form a single regulatory architecture, and that their combined effect is to convert the written record, the Form I-589 and its accompanying documentary evidence, from a supporting element of the asylum claim into the entire basis on which a case may be moved into removal proceedings. The paper further argues that this shift exposes a structural blind spot in immigration practice that predates the July rule and is not unique to Venezuela. Reviewing the standard training materials used by immigration practitioners, the paper finds a near-exclusive focus on procedural compliance, filing deadlines, declaration architecture, and hearing preparation, with no comparable body of practice guidance on the forensic authentication of foreign institutional documents. This gap has been tolerated because the asylum interview functioned, often without anyone naming it as such, as an informal corrective filter. That filter is now absent for a defined category of cases. The paper extends the seven-step due diligence framework proposed in the author's prior working paper from a post-filing review tool into a pre-filing diligence standard, and situates Venezuela within a broader group of high-volume origin countries, including Cuba, Nicaragua, Haiti, and Honduras, that share the same underlying condition of unreliable or uncooperative civil documentation systems.

title: Index Exclusion and the Supranational Safe-asset Premiun: Evidence from EU Bond Markets
affiliations: and Shahjalal University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Index Exclusion and the Supranational Safe-asset Premiun: Evidence from EU Bond Markets
detail.abstract: This thesis explores whether this contraction of the premium on safe assets, excluding EU bonds, leads to a rise in the premium on the AAA category and whether it is via a demand substitution channel. Two natural experiments are June 2024 rejection by MSCI and August 2025 rejection by ICE. This study will look at the time in which investors had to seek advice from MSCI on whether to stay or get out of the fund, a pre-announcement identification window. The window comes 16 days before the French snap vote. The central estimates of the AAA-Bund spread and the ten-year spread rose by 7.30 basis points (p<0.001) and 2.02 basis points (p=0.001) respectively between 1st and 24th May 2024. 30-year outcome is higher than all 5,000 permutation placebo benchmarks. More importantly, French OAT spreads were also narrowed by 7.11 basis points on thirty years over the same period, something that would not have been possible if capital had been flowing into EU supranationals, but would have happened if it had been flowing into French supranationals. The consultation period (1990 to 2006) coincides with a period of abnormal spread volatility at thirty years (F = 4.08, p < 0.001) as would be expected under institutional rebalancing. The results confirm the hypothesis that supranational safe asset premium is created through the demand substitution effect, which has a long-maturity focus, and extend the growing body of literature on European bond market segmentation with results from an exercise employing natural experiments.

title: UNFCITC Protocol on the Taxation of Cross-Border Services: A Primer of the Fifth Session Zero-Draft
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: UNFCITC Protocol on the Taxation of Cross-Border Services: A Primer of the Fifth Session Zero-Draft

keywords: Un Framework Convention in International Tax Cooperation

detail.abstract:
On 20 July 2026, the Co-Lead of Workstream 2 on the Protocol on the Taxation of Income from Cross-Border Services released the draft text of the protocol, the first protocol under the upcoming United Nations Framework Convention on International Tax Negotiation (UNFICTC).
In this primer, the author looks at what’s what in the twenty-two articles that make up the heavily anticipated protocol draft. The purpose of this to report is to unpack the in’s and out’s of the draft proposal for a wider audience, making up for the fact that the draft has been proposed without a formal ‘commentary’ or ‘technical explanation’. To judge the draft proposal’s on its merits, it is therefore useful to gather a better technical understanding of its proposed rules and their implications or shortcomings.
Structurally, the draft proposal looks like a stylized and multilateral version of a standard bilateral tax treaty. It contains the full tax treaty infrastructure, ranging from provisions on scope (taxes and taxpayers are covered), definitions, distributional rules that determine which country restricts its power to tax, rules on relief of double taxation in case of overlapping taxing claims, and special provisions on dispute settlement and administrative assistance.
While the release of the protocol text is an important moment in the negotiations, it is very much a zero-draft meant to be kneaded and kneaded again in the upcoming negotiation sessions.
The paper goes over the provisions of the draft protocol to give some context and to identify some important novelties and gaps that those negotiations may need to fill.

title: The Post-Capture Window: Institutionalizing Venezuelan Criminal Record Cooperation Before It Closes

detail.title: The Post-Capture Window: Institutionalizing Venezuelan Criminal Record Cooperation Before It Closes
detail.abstract: On January 3, 2026, United States forces captured Nicolás Maduro in Caracas as part of Operation Absolute Resolve, and the Southern District of New York unsealed an indictment naming, among Maduro's co-defendants, Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, alias Niño Guerrero, the founder and leader of Tren de Aragua. That indictment, placing a head of state and the leader of a transnational criminal organization in the same charging document, is the structural starting point of this paper. In the months that followed, the United States and the Venezuelan transitional government under acting President Delcy Rodríguez restored diplomatic relations, coordinated the extradition of a terrorism suspect to Panama, and, on June 12, 2026, executed a joint intelligence and kinetic operation that killed Niño Guerrero at a Tren de Aragua compound in Bolívar state, with Rodríguez's government publicly confirming that Venezuela supplied the intelligence that located him. This paper argues that these events demonstrate a functioning, if informal, channel of security cooperation between Washington and Caracas, and that this channel has not been extended to the one domain where its absence carries the highest cumulative cost for the United States, the systematic verification of Venezuelan nationals' criminal records for immigration, asylum, and law enforcement purposes. The paper traces the cooperation that now exists, identifies why it remains operation-specific rather than institutional, and proposes a concrete mechanism, the Venezuelan Criminal Record Verification Program, first outlined by the author in his 2026 book on Tren de Aragua, as the structure capable of converting a fragile, personality-dependent cooperation into a durable institutional channel before the political window that opened on January 3, 2026 closes.

title: Gig Economy Expansion and the Decline of Labor Market Power: Evidence from China
affiliations: Peking University - School of Economics, Peking University School of Economics,  and Peking University

detail.title: Gig Economy Expansion and the Decline of Labor Market Power: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the expansion of the gig economy reduces employers' labor market power. Using firm-level data from China spanning 2007 to 2020 and exploiting the staggered rollout of online food-delivery platforms across cities, we estimate that gig economy entry reduces manufacturing firms' wage markdowns by 6.94 percent. The mechanism operates through a compensation floor: gig work provides an outside option that workers exercise without separating from their employers, and firms raise both pay and employment in response. The effect is concentrated among low-paying firms and those providing little social insurance. We find no role for worker bargaining power and no support for alternative explanations related to declining productivity, workforce composition, or new business formation.

title: Probing the Slow Variable: A Preliminary Position Paper on Observability and the Allocation of Supervisory Duty in Organisations

detail.title: Probing the Slow Variable: A Preliminary Position Paper on Observability and the Allocation of Supervisory Duty in Organisations
detail.abstract: A supervisory obligation addressed to the stability of a social system presupposes that the condition of that system is available to some party. This paper asks whether it is available, at what cost, and to whom. The standard measurement applies a controlled disturbance and reads the recovery. Three results bear against it. In a bistable system under slow forcing the signal available from a probe grows with the recovery time while the amplitude that leaves the basin intact falls with the margin, and the product remains bounded, so the signal obtainable from a harmless probe fails to increase as the system deteriorates. A probe reaches the linearisation of the flow at the attractor and reaches no further, so the passage from what it recovers to the margin rests on an assumption about the class of the system, and disturbances arriving in the directions a setting happens to produce leave the estimate deficient in the directions along which nothing has yet occurred. And the burden of an applied disturbance falls most heavily on the member nearest the boundary, who is the member the measurement most concerns. Three ethical grounds are stated separately, since a reader who rejects the first result should still find applied probing unavailable. From these the paper derives the standing of passive measurement, which reads disturbances that occur without intervention and carries no marginal burden, and identifies the one form of applied probing that remains, namely the probing of the organisation's own response pathway rather than of its members. A further limit is then developed. A recovery interval is judged and not read off, and the account of the person concerned is exposed to discounting of credibility and to the absence of any term for a return that is incomplete. Both operations shorten the recorded interval, both act most strongly on those whose accounts are least credited, and those are the members nearest the boundary, so the instrument is biased in the direction that conceals the danger. The paper argues that observability is a positional property and that its distribution supplies a ground for allocating supervisory duty distinct from control and from advantage in information, relocates the assessment of foreseeability accordingly, and states the costs and the principal failure mode.

title: The Power Resources of Capital and the Struggle over Development in Argentina (2016-2026)
affiliations: and Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP)

detail.title: The Power Resources of Capital and the Struggle over Development in Argentina (2016-2026)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest. This research received no personal or financial support from any organization that could be perceived as having influenced the study
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based on the analysis of publicly available documents and secondary aggregate data, and did not involve human participants, human data, or animals.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (CONICET), Argentina. This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The Power Resources Approach (PRA) has become a key framework for analysing workers' collective power, yet it has rarely been applied to the capitalist class. This paper develops a symmetrical extension of the PRA to map the structural, associational, institutional, and societal power resources of dominant capital fractions. Empirically, we examine Argentina between 2016 and 2026, a period spanning three contrasting political projects: the neoliberal Cambiemos government (2016-2019), the structurally constrained national-popular Frente de Todos (2020-2023), and the radical free-market programme of Milei (2024-present). Drawing on national accounts, sectoral data, capital flight records, and discourse analysis, we demonstrate how large-scale capital deployed mutually reinforcing power resources to impose regressive redistribution, consolidate anti-populist hegemony, and, under Milei, translate longstanding discursive demands into sweeping institutional reform. The peripheral condition amplifies class power from above through dependency-enhanced structural mechanisms.

title: Causal Sufficiency and Structural Vulnerability: Rethinking Responsibility in Generative Relational Systems: A Preliminary Position Paper on the Foundations of Structural Attribution

detail.title: Causal Sufficiency and Structural Vulnerability: Rethinking Responsibility in Generative Relational Systems: A Preliminary Position Paper on the Foundations of Structural Attribution
detail.abstract: Two companion papers establish that in one class of injury the classical apparatus of causal attribution fails, and that the failure is of two kinds, one of resources and one of what a determinate contribution would require of any tribunal. Where causal sufficiency is unattainable, responsibility theory may turn to the structure of the relational system and ask which transformations of that structure a party brought about. This paper recapitulates those problems, separates the operation of law from the justice of its results, and examines whether the turn can be made. It offers no rule for deriving a share of responsibility from a structural change, and it holds that none is presently available. Its claims are four. The object of an attributive enquiry may be relocated from the production of an outcome to the production of a vulnerability, and the relocation is intelligible independently of any measure of contribution. A description of structural change is by itself normatively inert, since organisational reform alters connectivity, feedback and reachability in the same registers as degradation does, and no quantity computed on the structure distinguishes the two. A criterion is therefore required, and the paper proposes a candidate: a structural change carries normative weight where it removes the paths by which that very change could be contested and reversed. The candidate is self-referential where the alternatives are not, since a change leaving the channel of its own correction intact remains corrigible whatever else it does, and two changes to one structure are exhibited that agree on size, density and connectedness and differ only in whether the path of contestation survives. The invariants employed are then defined in the standard way, as quantities equal on topologically equivalent flows, and a pair of dynamics is exhibited whose basins differ in the number of holes they contain, so that the register of loops is shown to carry structural and not quantitative information. A constructed case is then carried through both enquiries: over the weightings the record admits, the share attributed to each of two withdrawals occupies most of the available range, while membership of a minimal cut is settled for all three. Finally the paper states what a finding on an invariant contributes and what it withholds. It contributes a finite evidentiary task, robustness to the strengths, rates and couplings a record leaves open, order-independent composition, and an identification of the parties concerned through the minimal sets of relations whose removal destroys the path. It withholds a share, it moves the requirement of closure from variables to positions rather than escaping it, it purchases invariance by discarding the difference between a channel that functions and one that is nominal, it leaves the minimal set undetermined where the record is incomplete, and it is silent on time. The proposal is offered as a constraint on attribution rather than as a procedure for it.

title: Labor Payments after Mergers and Acquisitions: Evidence from China
affiliations: , , , Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Academy of Mathematics and Systems Sciences and Harbin Institute of Technology

declarations.funderStatement: The authors gratefully acknowledge financial support from the Major Program of the National Social Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 23&ZD040, Study on Optimizing the Layout of Major Productive Forces in the New Development Phase) and the 2026 Research Project of the National Data Administration (Study on the Relationship between Inputs and Outputs in Digital Transformation).

detail.abstract: This paper examines employee-related cash payments after mergers and acquisitions (M&A) in China's policy-guided restructuring environment. State Council guidelines issued in 2010 and 2014 promoted enterprise restructuring while emphasizing employee settlement, the transfer of labor relations, and workforce stability. Using a matched event-study design, we find that acquirers increase cash paid to and on behalf of employees by 13.1% after M&A completion. The increase emerges in the completion year, persists for at least two years and is stronger for economically important transactions and state-influenced acquirers. We do not detect a comparable increase in the pre-2014 placebo sample. M&A completion is also associated with higher social ESG scores, lower governance scores, and lower Tobin's Q, while overall ESG scores and accounting profitability do not change significantly. These findings document the labor-payment implications of post-merger integration and highlight a potential trade-off between stakeholder protection and shareholder value.

title: A Rebate, Not a Match: A Systematic Literature Review of the Behavioral Economics of Charitable Giving and Its Implications for Tax Credit Fundraising
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Rebate, Not a Match: A Systematic Literature Review of the Behavioral Economics of Charitable Giving and Its Implications for Tax Credit Fundraising

detail.abstract: Few charitable incentives are as generous as Arizona's Foster Care Tax Credit, which returns every dollar a donor gives. This review asks whether that generosity could go further, not by changing the credit, but by changing how it is presented to donors. Drawing on 33 studies identified through a systematic search of five databases and grouped into six themes, it examines which behavioral mechanisms most strongly move charitable giving. Across that literature, donors respond to how a gift is framed and delivered more than to what it costs them. The clearest case is the comparison between matching subsidies and rebates, where a recent meta-analysis of 151 estimates found matching roughly twice as powerful as an economically identical rebate. Evidence from state credits points the same way. Iowa's 25 percent credit raised contributions to targeted nonprofits by 125 percent, while Arizona's 100 percent credit produced no significant increase, and a field experiment found that informing Arizona residents about the credit shifted giving toward qualifying charities without raising the total. The difference, this review argues, is structural rather than a matter of generosity, and the lever available to fundraisers is presentation, describing the state's return so it mirrors a match as closely as the truth allows, a gift the donor makes and the state meets, rather than as a refund claimed months later. No study has tested how a full dollar for dollar rebate should be framed to donors, including whether presenting it in the structure of a match raises giving, or examined this question in foster care, which marks a clear opening for future research.

title: Pension Reforms in Inheritance Societies
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - Finance Department

detail.title: Pension Reforms in Inheritance Societies
detail.abstract: This paper studies how pay-as-you-go pension systems shape the distribution of wealth across cohorts and amplify the role of inheritance when economic growth declines. A growth slowdown opens a budgetary gap, and when governments close it by raising contribution rates rather than cutting benefits, the net wages of workers fall while the resources of retirees are preserved. Slow growth therefore tilts wealth toward the elderly, the more so the more generous the pension system. Household data from twenty European countries confirm these predictions: the elderly are wealthiest relative to the working-age population where pensions are generous, especially where productivity growth has been slow. Furthermore, retiring cohorts accumulated wealth fastest in generous, slow-growth countries during the 2010-2023 slowdown. These trends shift national wealth shares from late-career households to those above seventy.

title: Reconstructing Generative Structure from Relational Trajectories: A Conformance Specification for the Study of Systems That Generate Their Own Units

detail.title: Reconstructing Generative Structure from Relational Trajectories: A Conformance Specification for the Study of Systems That Generate Their Own Units
detail.abstract: In a class of research objects the unit of analysis is produced by the process under study, and existing method treats the stability of that unit as a precondition to be checked rather than as an object to be modelled. Claims about change in such objects are therefore in part artefacts of the analyst's choice of unit, and no prevailing reporting norm requires anyone to say so. This paper offers one specification, not a method, for research on such objects. Three declarations are identified that no current standard requires: how the unit under comparison came to exist, how a variable at one scale is produced by and constrains another, and what an account of a process forbids. A formal presentation is then given in which a trajectory becomes analysable only under a declared partition of the state space; the grammar is stratified into epochs within which the production set is held fixed, with rewriting of the production set confined to epoch boundaries; non-terminals carry a scale index, so that the crossing of scales becomes a syntactic property open to audit; and the presentation is probabilistic, which is what makes model comparison well defined where only positive evidence exists. Three propositions follow. Membership is decidable within an epoch and undecidable if rewriting is permitted mid-derivation, which is why stratification is forced rather than stylistic. Acceptance under one partition entails nothing under a partition that does not refine it. A grammar containing no scale-crossing production derives no observation from a macro-level start symbol, so a claim to connect scales is checkable on the production set alone. The specification then states eight declarations that any implementation owes its reader, graded into requirements and recommendations, and it fixes which choices it leaves to the implementation. It is illustrated on a single trajectory. What the specification excludes, and the conditions under which each of its claims would fail, are stated at the end.

title: Zero-Copy Camera-to-NPU Preprocessing for Energy-Efficient Face Recognition on Ultra-Low-Cost Edge AI SoCs

detail.title: Zero-Copy Camera-to-NPU Preprocessing for Energy-Efficient Face Recognition on Ultra-Low-Cost Edge AI SoCs
detail.abstract: Low-cost edge vision systems must execute complete recognition pipelines under tight compute, memory, and power budgets. We show that, after neural inference is offloaded to a neural processing unit (NPU), camera-to-tensor preprocessing can dominate latency. On a 64-MB Rockchip RV1103, OpenCV detector preprocessing required 106--114 ms per frame, compared with 31--36 ms for NPU inference. We restructure buffer ownership across the video decoder, raster accelerator, and NPU runtime: decoded DMA-buf frames are imported directly by the raster accelerator, which converts and resizes them into RKNN-owned input memory. This reduces preprocessing to 3.0--3.5 ms and increases complete-pipeline throughput from about 5.6 FPS to 14--16 FPS across RetinaFace and SCRFD. Evaluated detection and paired verification protocols showed no statistically significant degradation. A complete optimized deployment profile improved board-level FPS/W by 3.37× on repeated workloads and 2.64× on a long-video workload. These results identify memory ownership and accelerator interoperability as central design concerns for ultra-low-cost edge AI.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates how Canada can convert the Canada Strong Fund, announced in April 2026 with $25 billion in seed capital, into a durable sovereign investment institution. It argues that the principal design problem is not access to capital but the coexistence of commercial return, domestic strategic investment, intergenerational saving, federalism and retail principal protection within one public vehicle. The paper classifies the announced fund as a strategic investment fund and recommends a dedicated statute, an independent skills-based board, a verified additionality test and three legally ring-fenced portfolios: a commercial Strategic Equity Portfolio, a globally diversified Intergenerational Reserve and a separately capitalized Retail Participation Trust. It further proposes transparent treatment of guarantees and below-market policy costs, voluntary provincial participation, structural Indigenous participation, explicit portfolio limits and public reporting against commercial, fiscal and strategic benchmarks. Comparative analysis of leading sovereign and public-investment institutions shows that legal clarity, mandate discipline and allocation of decision rights matter more than launch scale. Canada can enact the recommended architecture through ordinary federal legislation and voluntary intergovernmental agreements, without constitutional amendment or referendum. The central conclusion is that Canada should proceed, but statutory governance and portfolio separation must precede material capital deployment.

title: Capital-Intensive versus Researcher-Based R&D: Implications for Innovation Policy
affiliations: Azerbaijan State University of Economics (UNEC) - Scientific-Research Institute and Azerbaijan State University of Economics (UNEC) - Scientific-Research Institute

detail.title: Capital-Intensive versus Researcher-Based R&D: Implications for Innovation Policy
detail.abstract: A substantial body of literature emphasizes technological progress as a key driver of long-run productivity growth, yet comparatively little attention is paid to the composition of R&D activities-specifically, the relative roles of capital-intensive and researcher-based R&D. This paper argues that, despite the key role researchers play in technological progress, firms tend to favor capitalintensive R&D over researcher-based R&D. The paper examines the factors underlying this preference and argues that, to support technological progress and long-term productivity growth, innovation policy should focus on stimulating researcher employment rather than aggregate R&D expenditure.

title: GenAI Governance in School: How Guidelines and Enforcement Shape Student Performance
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST), affiliation not provided to SSRN and

detail.title: GenAI Governance in School: How Guidelines and Enforcement Shape Student Performance
detail.abstract: Schools have responded to Generative AI with two main strategies: teaching students to use it responsibly through instructional guidelines, and capping AI-generated content with enforcement. Yet there is little causal evidence on the effects of these policies in real classrooms. We run a randomized controlled trial across two Chinese middle schools (N = 1,056), cross-randomizing a six-module AI literacy curriculum with an enforcement intervention that imposes a 30% AI-content cap on writing assignments, detects violations through multi-engine AI screening with instructor verification, and mandates resubmission for flagged submissions. Neither component alone generates detectable academic gains, while the combination of guidelines and enforcement improves writing performance, particularly Chinese writing. The writing gains are concentrated among male students. Compliance outcomes suggest gender-specific behavioral responses to the policy environment. Under guidelines alone, female students reduce measured AI violations, whereas male students' violation rates remain higher than in other conditions. Therefore, guidelines without enforcement, the most common policy responses to AI in schools, may backfire unless accompanied by a well-designed compliance mechanism.

title:
Resources Change Hands, Capability Does Not 
A Low-Capability Equilibrium and Eighty Years of British Reform
affiliations: Strategic Policy Research, Inc.

detail.title:
Resources Change Hands, Capability Does Not 
A Low-Capability Equilibrium and Eighty Years of British Reform
detail.abstract:
Since 1945 Britain has alternated repeatedly between two opposed policy paradigmspostwar state ownership and Thatcherite market liberalism-and yet every reform wave has reproduced the same territorial imbalance: a hyper-capable centre and a hollowed periphery. This paper asks why. It argues that the recurrence is not a sequence of policy mistakes but a stable, self-reinforcing equilibrium, and that its persistence follows from a single, generalisable proposition: states can change who allocates resources far more easily than they can change where capability is generated.
The asymmetry has a mechanism: capability is generated only through institutional learning under responsibility that cannot be shifted elsewhere, whereas ownership can be altered by legislation, so the two move at entirely different speeds. Reform in Britain has repeatedly changed the resource-allocation paradigm — who owns and directs the economy — while leaving untouched the capability-generation mechanism, which has remained monopolised at the centre throughout. Drawing a distinction between central and distributed state capability, and extending Michael Mann’s concept of infrastructural power one step further to locally generated capability, the paper supplies a behavioural microfoundation (capability accrues through institutional learning under responsibility that cannot be shifted elsewhere), models the recurrence as a low distributed-capability equilibrium, and states the conditions under which the theory would be falsified. It then tests the mechanism against eighty years of British experience — five “doses,” one equilibrium — using Germany as a comparative counter-curve, and shows how successive governing coalitions, though they change, each inherit and reinforce the same central machine. The paper closes by arguing that the fiscal crisis of the 2020s is, for the first time in eighty years, an exogenous shock of the kind that could make fiscal devolution rational for the centre itself rather than merely desirable to the periphery — a prediction, and offered as such — and by drawing out what the proposition predicts for other centralised states. Britain is treated throughout not as an object of national-declinist commentary but as the clearest, best-documented instance of a general law.

title: Western Electronics Inside Sanctioned Russian Weapons: The Hong Kong Route That Won't Close

detail.title: Western Electronics Inside Sanctioned Russian Weapons: The Hong Kong Route That Won't Close
detail.abstract: This brief investigates how Western-made microelectronics continue reaching Russian precision-guided missile and drone programs more than four years into sanctions on their export. Drawing on U.S. Treasury, Commerce, and Justice Department enforcement actions, European Union sanctions designations, and independently corroborated investigative research, it maps a durable Hong Kong-centered trading network responsible for documented shipments of Tier 1 controlled components to sanctioned Russian entities. The analysis identifies the structural mechanism enabling this persistence: a distributor visibility gap in which compliance obligations end one sale before a component's actual destination is determined. Six enforcement actions across four jurisdictions since 2024 are examined in sequence, alongside named on-record analysis from sanctions researchers describing the same failure from the manufacturer's side. The brief argues that closing this gap requires extending verification obligations one tier further down the distribution chain rather than tightening controls at the point of first sale, which current evidence shows is already functioning as intended.

title: Riding Behaviour of Commercial Delivery Motorcyclists Measured with Smartphone and Sensor-Tag Telematics: Event Rates and a Combined Rider Behaviour Model
affiliations: Stellenbosch University, Stellenbosch University, World Bank Group and Stellenbosch University - Faculty of Engineering

detail.title: Riding Behaviour of Commercial Delivery Motorcyclists Measured with Smartphone and Sensor-Tag Telematics: Event Rates and a Combined Rider Behaviour Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a secondary analysis of telematics data collected by the SSATP/World Bank pilot and captured by a commercial insurance provider (Discovery Insure, South Africa) and made available to the authors under a data-sharing agreement with the SSATP program (through the World Bank) and Discovery Insurance. Written informed consent for data collection and research use was obtained from all riders by the SSATP pilot at the point of original data collection. Author two was present during data collection to oversee compliance and holds the signed consent documentation on this basis; he did not take part in the data analysis. The data used for analysis was fully anonymised, and the analysing authors had no access to identifying information and no direct contact with participants.
declarations.funderStatement: World Bank Group.

detail.abstract: Naturalistic driving studies rely on thresholds that separate an ordinary manoeuvre from a hard one, yet for powered two-wheelers this boundary is unresolved: published triggers vary by an order of magnitude and none are derived from the vehicle or population studied. We address this gap with a rider behaviour model that detects, verifies, and grades five naturalistic riding behaviours, acceleration, braking, cornering, speeding, and stop compliance, using smartphone and vehicle-tag telematics from a fleet of 28 commercial delivery motorcyclists in Stellenbosch, South Africa. Each behaviour is scored by a detector that selects the signal and metric suited to it, isolates events, verifies each against a second signal or internal consistency, grades severity on a scale frozen from the fleet's own range, and aggregates events into an unweighted score out of 100. Applying this model to 1,382 acceleration and braking events over 17,196 qualitygated kilometres, 1,153 pass verification; 23 of 28 riders are scored on this behaviour and 19 on stop compliance. Acceleration and braking scores correlate only weakly across riders (0.29), so harshness in one does not predict harshness in the other; three tracked riders show a comparable crossover across all five behaviours, with no rider uniformly best or worst. The frozen braking and acceleration scales land within published motorcyclist deceleration and naturalistic-use ranges, validating thresholds set without prior literature; percentile-sweep and split-window checks show rankings are stable and recur over time for the better-populated behaviours. This evidenceanchored approach offers a transferable methodology for naturalistic powered-two-wheeler risk scoring.

title: Analysis of Influencing Factors of Farmland Pollination Services: Cross-Level Moderating Effects of Farmers and Villages
affiliations: Inner Mongolia Normal University, Inner Mongolia Normal University and Inner Mongolia Normal University

detail.title: Analysis of Influencing Factors of Farmland Pollination Services: Cross-Level Moderating Effects of Farmers and Villages
detail.abstract: Pollination services, as a core ecosystem service bridging natural ecology and agricultural production, play an irreplaceable role in safeguarding food security and driving green agricultural transformation. However, in village-level agricultural landscapes dominated by smallholder dispersed farming, the farmlands managed by individual households and the semi-natural habitats within village boundaries collectively form a mosaic landscape pattern. This causes the supply and maintenance of farmland pollination services to be simultaneously influenced by factors at both the household and village levels, exhibiting a typical double-layer nested characteristic. Yet research specifically addressing this feature remains scarce. Based on field surveys and household questionnaire data from 480 households across 22 villages in Dengkou County, Inner Mongolia, this study calculated a household-level pollination service index and a village-level semi-natural habitat pollination potential index, collected additional factors at both levels, and employed Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM) to disentangle the independent effects of the household and village levels while testing cross-level interaction effects on pollination services. The results show that village-level variation accounts for 6.9% of the total variance in pollination services, confirming the necessity of the nested structure. Household behaviors such as retaining wildflowers and keeping bees independently significantly enhance pollination services. The village-level semi-natural habitat pollination potential index, crop diversity, and the proportion of cooperative beekeeping all show significant positive effects. More importantly, cross-level interaction analysis reveals two distinct moderating mechanisms—substitution effects and synergy effects—indicating that the same household behavior produces differentiated ecological outcomes across villages with different landscape contexts. Our findings underscore the need to incorporate household environmentally friendly behaviors into ecological subsidy programs, and to leverage land consolidation and ecological restoration policies to promote semi-natural habitat construction through village-specific classification based on resource endowment differences, thereby enhancing pollination services. This study provides empirical evidence for the precise design of agro-ecological conservation policies under smallholder farming systems and offers reference for other developing countries exploring synergies between ecology and agriculture.

title: Goals of the Afcfta Competition Protocol Digital Marketcompetition Regulations: Lessons from South Africa's Online Intermediation Platform Market Inquiry (OIPMI), The Eu's Dma and the Us Experiences with Digital Platform Giants
affiliations: Technische Universität München (TUM) and

detail.title: Goals of the Afcfta Competition Protocol Digital Marketcompetition Regulations: Lessons from South Africa's Online Intermediation Platform Market Inquiry (OIPMI), The Eu's Dma and the Us Experiences with Digital Platform Giants
detail.abstract: The European Union (EU) has continued to be a worldwide leader in setting international norms, particularly in competition law policy, data protection and platform governance. In digital market regulation, after the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA), several countries have adopted or are considering the adoption of digital markets competition regulations (DMCR) similar to the DMA. While some have challenged the notion that the DMA and its goals of ensuring contestability and fairness in the market should not be the blueprint for adopting DMCRs in other countries, at this juncture, it is impossible to overstate the influence of the EU DMA on future DMCRs. We contribute towards this scholarly debate on the influence of the DMA beyond the EU by focusing on a region that, despite competition agencies’ regulatory enforcement in digital markets, has not received adequate scholarly attention: Africa. Although no African country has considered adopting a DMCR at the continental level, African countries seek to adopt a DMCR under the AfCFTA Competition Protocol (CP). In formulating the appropriate goals of the AfCFTA DMCR, we build on African experiences in enforcing competition law, the African market structure, the debate on the goals of competition law in Africa, intellectual thinking on regulation of digital markets and the EU DMA. More specifically, for the African context, we draw on the 2023 Competition Commission of South Africa, Online Intermediation Platforms Market Inquiry (OIPMI) findings on business user treatment to further inform the appropriate goals of the AfCFTA DMCR. An analysis of the OIPMI Final Report shows that African markets have high barriers to entry, and digital platforms impose unfair trading conditions on African businesses compared to international businesses. Consequently, like the EU DMA, fairness and contestability are critical for the success of African businesses in the digital markets. Given that public interest considerations will continue to shape African competition law enforcement in digital markets, African countries can draw from the insights of the EU Ordoliberal thinking as related to the currently dissipated US New Brandeisian movement, both of which seek to enhance the participation of small businesses in a market characterized by few firms with concentrated economic power. We conclude by recommending that, unlike the DMA, in which the goals are distinct from competition law, the AfCFTA DMCR should incorporate multiple goals merging regulatory goals with those of competition law enforcement, while prioritizing innovation, inclusivity, fairness, and contestability.

title: The Law of the Algorithmic State in Central and Eastern Europe
