detail.abstract:
Section 301 China tariffs matter because they represent a major recent intervention in U.S. manufacturing trade policy, with potential implications for domestic production, prices, and shipments. According to textbook trade theory, tariffs are intended to support the domestic economy by raising the relative cost of foreign goods and services, thereby protecting import-competing domestic producers from foreign competition. This paper uses the 2018–2019 Section 301 tariffs on Chinese imports as a source of exogenous variation to estimate the effects of these tariffs on production, prices, and shipments in the U.S. economy. The paper uses a triple-difference design at the NAICS-4 level, with world import penetration as the control dimension, and analyzes three outcome panels: BLS-PPI, FRED-IP, and Census-M3. The estimation using the FRED-IP panel indicates that tariff exposure reduced manufacturing activity: β = −0.783 and boot-p = 0.005, with an attenuation ratio of 1.016. Practically, at the mean exposure level among treated industries, the estimated effect corresponds to an approximate 17.7 percent reduction in industrial production after the tariff shock (see Appendix A7).

Methodologically, I use a three-difference-in-differences approach to compare high-exposure versus low-exposure industries before and after the tariff shocks; the third difference corresponds to the level of penetration of non-Chinese goods to account for pre-trends across a family of commodities. When the effect of tariffs on prices was examined, the results indicated a positive but imprecise effect, which may reflect insufficient variation at the industry level; nevertheless, the clustered standard errors detected a statistically significant relationship, though this relationship became imprecise under bootstrap inference. In the primary specification, Census-M3 shows a negative effect on nominal shipments (attenuation ratio of −0.961), although this estimate is imprecisely estimated.

The paper contributes evidence on how tariff shocks propagate across production, prices, and shipments within manufacturing industries. In doing so, it complements research on the price and welfare incidence of the 2018–2019 tariffs by adding production-side evidence at the NAICS-4 level, contributes to the broader literature on how tariff and import-competition shocks propagate through domestic manufacturing, and offers a triple-difference design with a continuous world-import-penetration control as an alternative to more conventional binary treatment definitions.

title: Industrial Subsidies and Global Market Shares: A First Principles Analysis

detail.title: Industrial Subsidies and Global Market Shares: A First Principles Analysis
detail.abstract: Industrial subsidies have returned to the centre of international economic policy debates following publication of results based on the OECD's MAGIC database that subsidies accounted for a substantial share of manufacturing firm's market-share gains over the period 2005-2023, particularly those of Chinese firms. Taking the OECD's subsidy estimates as given, this paper reconsiders their economic significance from first principles. In line with the OECD's observation that the impact of subsidies flows through firms' effective weighted average cost of capital (WACC) to increased investment, the paper translates the subsidies expressed as a share of revenue, as presented by the OECD, into equivalent reductions in financing costs. Applying representative financial data for the United States, Europe and China, the paper shows that the implied reductions in country-average WACCs, while economically meaningful, remain modest relative to the dispersion of financing costs observed across industries and still leave China with a higher average cost of capital. The paper further observes that gross subsidies cannot be interpreted independently of taxation and other fiscal transfers (what matters is the un-measured net fiscal transfer), distinguishes reductions in WACC from reductions in investment hurdle rates in driving investment, and highlights the functional equivalence of "soft budget constraints" faced by state-owned enterprises with the weak conditionality on profits when private capital is supported by deep capital markets and "plutocratic capital". Finally, it argues that Lerner symmetry cautions against interpreting export market-share gains as deriving from subsidies without accounting for corresponding effects of subsidies on imports. As a bottom line, the paper argues that the OECD's non-findings of any meaningful impact of subsidies on firm investment rates, productivity or profitability undermine its conclusion that subsidies nonetheless had a massive impact on firms' market shares; and advances the conjecture that the market share gains of Chinese firms were explained principally by the expansion of China's economy and that the role of the state ran not through subsidies that reduced the WACC but through the reduction in the hurdle rate of investment, which enabled the rapid modernization of China's economy by substituting the socially optimal hurdle rate for the much higher private rate. The paper draws conclusions for the conduct of industrial policy by small open economies.

title: From Transmission Loss to Transmission Immunity: How Organizational Joints Reject or Defend Intent
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Transmission Loss to Transmission Immunity: How Organizational Joints Reject or Defend Intent
detail.abstract: Organizational intent frequently fails to translate into practice not merely due to signal attenuation during transmission, but active resistance. This paper introduces the construct of “transmission immunity” to capture mechanisms whereby organizational joints selectively filter, block or resist signals conflicting with incumbents‘ interests or value orientations. Building upon the Organizational Skeleton Framework, we argue that transmission immunity is inherently dual-sided. When joints are occupied by self-interested actors, malignant immunity emerges, repudiating official organizational intent and accelerating structural rigidity. When occupied by actors with strong organizational identification, benign immunity arises, enabling resistance to flawed top-down directives and safeguarding core organizational functions. Drawing on comparative case analyses of labour unions (CFMEU, PSA) and corporations (Toshiba, Enron), this article identifies triggering conditions, operational mechanisms and organizational outcomes of transmission immunity. Our analysis suggests that a functional organizational skeleton relies not only on formal structural design, but also on value alignment and feedback mechanisms embedded within its transmission joints.

detail.abstract: Academic societies distribute a consequential resource-seats on the bodies that govern a discipline-yet the historical composition of those bodies is rarely published, and longitudinal study has been correspondingly rare. This report reconstructs fourteen years of governance composition for a Japanese social-science society from public web archives, recovering eight consecutive terms (2012-2026) across every published layer, and reads that reconstruction against the society's articles of incorporation and electoral regulations. The society selects its governing bodies by election: members elect a body of delegates under a parallel system in which half the seats are apportioned across six districts in proportion to membership, and those delegates in turn elect the directors. The regulations, however, apportion the franchise and not eligibility. Every regular member is eligible for the directorate, and in each post-incorporation term between a quarter and a third of directors held no delegate seat. Regional diversity is accordingly stable at the base layer (Simpson's index 0.742 in 2012, 0.753 in the current term) but falls to 0.172 at the directorate and to 0.000 across the full published succession of presidents, every one of whom has been affiliated with an institution in a single district. The fall occurs at the layer at which the regional apportionment device ceases to apply.

title: Rising Inflation in India: Causes, Consequences and Policy Pathways -A Contemporary Review
affiliations: Awadhesh Pratap Singh University and  Government Thakur Ranmat Singh Autonomous College

detail.title: Rising Inflation in India: Causes, Consequences and Policy Pathways -A Contemporary Review
detail.abstract: Inflation has re-emerged as the central macroeconomic concern for Indian policymakers in 2026. Retail price inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), climbed steadily from historic lows recorded in mid-2025 to 4.38 per cent by June 2026, while wholesale price inflation, measured by the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), crossed 9.8 percent in the same month, the widest wholesaleretail divergence witnessed in several years. This review article examines the recent trajectory of inflation in India against the backdrop of the major theoretical traditions in the economics of inflation classical monetarism, Keynesian demand-management theory, cost-push and structuralist analysis, and the expectations-augmented Phillips Curveand situates the current episode within the specific conjuncture of a West Asian geopolitical shock, crude-oil price volatility, rupee depreciation and an uneven southwest monsoon. Drawing on official statistics released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, together with the published views of economists such as Raghuram Rajan and C. Rangarajan and the assessments of contemporary market economists, the article develops a comparative analysis of the causes, transmission channels and distributional consequences of the present inflationary episode, paying particular attention to its disproportionate burden on rural and low-income households. The review concludes with a synthesis of monetary, fiscal and supply-side policy recommendationsincluding calibrated repo-rate management, buffer-stock and agriculturalmarket reform, strategic energy reserves, exchange-rate stabilisation and targeted social protectionintended to restore price stability without unduly sacrificing India's underlying growth momentum. The analysis contributes to the ongoing academic and policy debate on inflation management in large emerging economies confronting simultaneous external shocks and structural rigidities.

title: Identifying Inventory Policies from Digital Traces: A Data-driven Approach using Real-World Order Patterns
affiliations: Kuehne Logistics University and Kuehne Logistics University

detail.title: Identifying Inventory Policies from Digital Traces: A Data-driven Approach using Real-World Order Patterns
detail.abstract: Understanding how inventory policies are implemented in practice remains a fundamental challenge in operations management because replenishment rules are rarely shared with others. However, different inventory policies leave identifiable signatures in transactional order data, creating an opportunity to infer otherwise hidden replenishment structures. This study develops a two-stage data-driven framework for identifying inventory policies directly from observed order behavior. In the first stage, semi-synthetic data, machine-learning classification, and expert evaluation are used to develop and validate a robust policy-identification model. In the second stage, the selected model is applied to a large-scale order dataset provided by a global travel-retail wholesaler, comprising 128,834 order time series across a diverse set of retailers and product categories. The results reveal only partial alignment between observed replenishment behavior and classical inventory-theory expectations. While policy selection varies systematically with product characteristics, substantial heterogeneity exists across retailers, and identical products are frequently managed using different replenishment rules. Retailer-level factors explain more variation in inferred policy behavior than product characteristics alone, highlighting the importance of organizational context in inventory-policy implementation. The study contributes a scalable methodology for inventory-policy identification and provides large-scale empirical evidence on how inventory policies are implemented in practice. More broadly, it demonstrates how the digital traces embedded in transactional order data can be used to uncover otherwise unobservable operational decision structures.

title: Chinese Automotive Brands in Europe: The Infrastructure Donor Trap and the Semiotic Barrier to Premiumization

detail.title: Chinese Automotive Brands in Europe: The Infrastructure Donor Trap and the Semiotic Barrier to Premiumization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests and no personal or institutional relationships that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it did not involve human participants, patients, animals, clinical intervention, or identifiable personal data.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a two-level hypothesis concerning structural barriers to premiumization of Chinese automotive brands in the European market. The first level is market-operational: Chinese groups build dealer networks, service infrastructure, and category familiarity, lowering the psychological entry barrier. However, at technological parity the accumulated infrastructure is inherited by European brands with established symbolic capital. The key donated asset is the charging network: Chinese brands deploy fast-charging stations continent-wide, creating brand-neutral contact points that benefit all compatible vehicles. This mechanism is termed the infrastructure donor trap. The second level is semiotic: the visual identities of key Chinese brands carry preconscious associative risks through three channels — visual gestalt (BYD, Denza, Yangwang, NIO, ORA, GWM, XPeng, Zeekr, Geely), lexical priming (NIO, MG), and phonetic priming (Xiaomi). Analysis is conducted through detailed verbal descriptions of geometric structure; no visual materials are reproduced. Comparative analysis of Korean brands establishes an asymmetry: Korean brands entered Europe with low logo-level risks and strong lexical priming from model names. Chinese brands entered with the inverse configuration. The paper documents analogous risks in established brands (Lexus, SEAT) and explains why the same mechanism produces different outcomes depending on accumulated symbolic capital — the suppression buffer. A five-stage clinical screening protocol (Kartashov, 2026a) is proposed as a universal detection instrument absent from current industry practice.

title: The Dobbs Dissent Delay: Examining Allegations of Intentional Delay Amid Threats to the Justices

detail.title: The Dobbs Dissent Delay: Examining Allegations of Intentional Delay Amid Threats to the Justices
detail.abstract: After the leaked draft opinion in Dobbs, the Justices in the majority faced threats, harassment, and at least one assassination attempt. Yet the Court did not release its decision until 205 days after oral argument, more than twice the average length of time. In 2026, conservative journalist Mollie Hemingway made the explosive allegation that despite this danger to their colleagues, the dissenting Justices intentionally delayed releasing their dissent through a series of calculated postponements, and then by inserting a single footnote to a not-yet-published Supreme Court opinion, thus further delaying the decision in Dobbs. This Article examines numerous aspects of that claim. After documenting the Dobbs case and subsequent leak, it considers the scope of the threats against the Justices in the majority and the dismissive response by some politicians, journalists, and law enforcement—context essential to evaluating the delay allegation. Next, it presents Hemingway’s allegation. Then, it assesses the strengths and weaknesses of the claim, considering the timeline, a parallel controversy in Louisiana v. Callais, the uncorroborated, single-source nature of the claim and related potential for a politically motivated bias by Hemingway, the unprecedented nature and length of the majority opinion that the dissent was responding to, the relative significance of dissenting opinions, the necessity of a footnote that caused further delays, and Chief Justice Roberts’s unwillingness to release the majority opinion early—something he did in another case three years earlier. This Article concludes that, while no direct evidence confirms an intentional delay, and there are numerous arguments against Hemingway’s claim, the circumstantial evidence lends the claim more credibility than it has thus far received. Finally, this Article examines potential mechanisms for accountability and concludes that none would be actionable.

title: CEO Personal Donating behavior and Corporate Social Responsibility
affiliations: University of Mississippi, University of Alabama and Liaoning University

detail.title: CEO Personal Donating behavior and Corporate Social Responsibility
detail.abstract: Using hand-collected data on CEOs' charitable donations, we show that firms led by CEOs who consistently donate exhibit significantly higher CSR performance than those led by occasional donors or non-donors. To identify causality, we examine exogenous CEO turnover events using a difference-indifferences approach and find that CSR performance increases when a non-routine-donor or non-donor CEO is replaced by a routine donor CEO and vice versa. These findings support behavioral consistency theory, indicating that CEOs' personal socially responsible behavior is indicative of their firms' CSR actions. Overall, we provide new evidence on why firms engage in CSR and identify a previously overlooked CEO attribute that helps explain CSR variation across firms.

title: Artificially Intelligent? Predicted Capability versus Observed Adoption in US Occupations

detail.title: Artificially Intelligent? Predicted Capability versus Observed Adoption in US Occupations

declarations.ethicsApproval: Note: the paper analyzes publicly released Anthropic data; the author has no affiliation with Anthropic.
declarations.funderStatement: There are no funding interests to declare.

detail.abstract: Using Anthropic's Economic Index-real AI usage mapped to O*NET taskswe characterize observed AI exposure across 756 US occupations and compare it with predicted capability. Exposure is a spike, not a wave: the median occupation shows zero observed exposure, and 86 percent of theoretically capable tasks show no observed use. Yet the spike stands on wide ground: employment-weighting raises mean exposure from 0.077 to 0.132, and roughly a quarter of covered US employment (~33 million jobs) sits in occupations where AI is observed performing over a quarter of the work-concentrated in large clerical and sales occupations, not software. Capability does not predict adoption: a permutation benchmark shows the occupation-level correlation with Eloundou et al.'s β (ρ = 0.71) is almost entirely generated by the measure's capability gate, and within the envelope, what predicts use is whether work already flows through a computer-teleworkable occupations occupy 11 points more of their envelope, while wages and capability gradations contribute little. The occupational map is robust: cross-vendor agreement with Microsoft's Copilot-based measure (0.58) matches cross-vintage agreement within Anthropic's (0.58), with category-level structure stable across both.

title: A Path to Customer-centric Marketing Mix Modeling

detail.title: A Path to Customer-centric Marketing Mix Modeling

detail.abstract: Customer-centric marketing decisions are vital for many companies to achieve sustainable customer growth. Most industry-standard solutions to the optimal marketing mix, however, focus on aggregate metrics such as revenue or orders to arrive at budget allocations across marketing channels. This disregards variations in customer quality by channel. Such a channel-centric approach might allocate budgets towards "quick-win" channels that frequently produce one-time or impulse buyers. A customer-centric approach determines how to allocate budgets across channels to attract the "right" customers, leading to more sustainable customer growth. This paper proposes concepts and methods for combining customer lifetime value calculation, insights from the customer centricity literature, and marketing mix modeling techniques to develop a framework for more customer-centric decision intelligence regarding the optimal marketing mix.

title: Shared Substrate: A Discipline for Sustained Human–AI Coupling on Complex Problems

detail.title: Shared Substrate: A Discipline for Sustained Human–AI Coupling on Complex Problems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This work was conducted independently; the discipline it articulates draws on the author's own practice across personal projects.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable: the paper is conceptual and involves no studies with patients or participants. The worked examples draw solely on the author's own professional practice.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Modern AI agents have characteristic limitations on long-horizon complex work: bounded context windows, drift across iterations, phantom decisions (claims of resolution not grounded in any artefact), reference rot, lost intent, and the cost of restarting cold each session. These limits will not be dissolved by larger models — they are limits of substrate, the externalised state any sustained reasoning must traverse. We articulate Shared Substrate: the discipline of forming, maintaining, and cascading hierarchical external representations across the manifestation trajectory of a project, made explicit here in response to the demands of multi-session AI collaboration. The organising image is the centroid: the participants in sustained work — the human operator, AI agents, successive model generations, colleagues — are noisy point masses in motion, and the substrate is the deliberately pinned centre of mass of that ensemble. Session drift is excursion; warm-up is reversion; the discipline is what holds the centroid stationary. The discipline rests on long-standing cognitive-science foundations — distributed cognition (Hutchins, 1995), external representations (Scaife and Rogers, 1996), cognitive load (Sweller, 1988), hierarchical levels of analysis (Marr, 1982), boundary objects (Star and Griesemer, 1989) — recovers software-engineering precedent (Architectural Decision Records (Nygard, 2011), Single Source of Truth, hexagonal architecture (Cockburn, 2005), append-only logs (Candea and Fox, 2003)) alongside emerging agentic-AI patterns (Lewis et al., 2020; Packer et al., 2024; Shinn et al., 2023; Bai et al., 2022), and is grounded formally: each abstraction layer of a project is paired with a representation formalism and a verification oracle — from executable behavioural contracts at the topmost layer to measurable non-functional envelopes at the operational one — with the work's state kept observable to the agents themselves, closing the feedback loop that enforces guardrails while divergence is still cheap to correct. The substrate that results is best understood as a compressed representation of the thing being manifested — agentic pipelines expand it into the work, and the human deposits only what no pipeline can derive — so the discipline's purpose has a one-line statement: separate genuine human creative input from cognitive load. The discipline defines six artefact categories — Knowledge Bases, Inventories, Data Dictionaries, Decision Records, Open Questions, Glossary — a status lifecycle, an edit protocol with explicit anti-patterns and a trivial-fix lane, and forward/reverse propagation rules across the hierarchy. Its posture is human-governed, agent-executed: a five-layer adoption stack progressively delegates substrate execution to agents while intent, decision, and scope authority remain with the person. The practice is domain-agnostic — software engineering appears here only as the worked instance — and practicable today with no special tooling. We claim the substrate matters as much as the model, and that this is the form of work AI raises in importance — not invents.

title:
The Universal Consumer 

 Six Philosophical Archetypes, Their Trigger Points, and a Cross-Archetype Strategy Under the IPPO Model

detail.title:
The Universal Consumer 

 Six Philosophical Archetypes, Their Trigger Points, and a Cross-Archetype Strategy Under the IPPO Model
detail.abstract:
Beyond the Funnel argued that consumer loyalty is the product of a four-layer psychological alignment — Interest, Personality, Philosophy, Outcome — rather than the terminal stage of a purchase funnel. This companion paper operationalizes that claim by proposing six universal consumer archetypes, each with its own trigger point, tailored marketing strategy, and characteristic vulnerability, unified by a single cross-archetype discipline, the Evidence Layer, which fails in six distinct, predictable ways when applied without adaptation.
Two prior rounds of structured external review established that an archetype is a state rather than a fixed trait — varying by product category, by culture along two independent axes, and by a customer's phase within an ongoing relationship — and built out a full validation roadmap, blended-profile map, B2B applicability, macroeconomic sensitivity, and measurement framework.
This third revised edition adds five further extensions. An Archetypal Friction Threshold formalizes what happens when acute economic or personal stress forces one archetypal driver to temporarily override another, with an override-resistance ranking across the six archetypes. Behavioural-proxy diagnosis is extended from web telemetry into phygital and physical-retail signals, and into real-time generative personalization — constrained by an explicit rule that automation may change how a verified claim is phrased, never what is claimed. The lifecycle model gains a set of Decay Signals for detecting phase regression before it becomes churn. And the B2B model gains a contract-closing playbook mapping archetype-driven objections at the final negotiation stage. 
The paper closes with the IPPO Consumer Archetype Diagnostic — an eight-item forced-choice instrument for directional use — together with a scoring key, an interpretation guide, and notes on administering it per category. A companion interactive version of the same instrument is provided alongside this paper.
